title: Markov Chain (S3) Class — new_MarkovChain
code: # Choose the transition probability matrix and the initial law of the MC a <- c(0.5, 0.5, 0) P <- matrix(c(0.3, 0.7, 0,               0.6, 0.1, 0.3,               0.5, 0,   0.5), nrow = 3, ncol = 3, byrow = TRUE)  # Create a Markov Chain x <- MarkovChain(a = a, P = P)  # Find Stationary distribution pi_vec <- mc_stat(x)  # Simulate a single trajectory of length m m <- 1e4 traj <- mc_sim(m, x)  # Estimate the transition probability matrix y <- mc_estim(traj)  # Make a list of Markov Chains L <- MarkovChainList(list(x, y)) L[[1]] #> Markov Chain #>   Number of states: 3  #>  #>   Initial distribution (a): #>       1   2   3  #>     0.5 0.5 0.0  #>  #>   Transition matrix (P): #>         1   2   3 #>     1 0.3 0.7 0.0 #>     2 0.6 0.1 0.3 #>     3 0.5 0.0 0.5

what: Availability of a Markov chain — avail
title: Availability of a Markov chain — avail
text: Compute discrete-time availability function system whose degradation/repair dynamics modeled finite-state Markov chain. Availability time \(t\) defined $$   (t) = \Pr\{ X_t \\mathcal{U} \} $$ \(X_t\) state chain time \(t\) \(\mathcal{U}\) set (operational) states. Equivalently, time \(t\) time, function computes $$   (t) = P^t \mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{U}}, $$ \(P = x$P\) transition matrix \(\mathbf{1}_{\mathcal{U}}\) indicator vector states.

text: numeric \(s \times s\) matrix, \(s\) number states, giving asymptotic covariance matrix \(\Sigma_\pi\).

title: Asymptotic Variance–Covariance Matrix of the stationary distribution MLE — var_stat
text: Let \(P\) transition matrix irreducible finite-state Markov chain stationary distribution \(\pi\). \(\hat P\) MLE \(P\) based long trajectory, induced estimator \(\hat\pi = \pi(\hat P)\) satisfies $$\sqrt{n}(\hat\pi - \pi) \xrightarrow{d} \mathcal{N}(0, \Sigma_\pi).$$ implementation uses delta method matrix form Kronecker: $$\Sigma_\pi = M\,\Gamma\,M^\top,$$ \(\Gamma\) asymptotic covariance matrix \(\mathrm{vec}(\hat P)\) returned mat_gamma(), $$M = \pi^\top \otimes (- P^\top + \mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^\top)^{-1}.$$
